title: Advice for New KFUPM Students
paragraphs: Are you a new student at KFUPM? Is this your first time away from home? Did you finish high school just a few months ago? If the answer to these questions is yes, you might be having a difficult time right now. It’s hard to be a new student! Many find it difficult being so far from home, or studying in English, or no longer always being the best in the class! Here’s some advice to help you deal with these problems.

When you’re away from home for the first time, it can be a sad and lonely time. But you should remember, these feelings usually only last a few weeks. Once you’ve made new friends, homesickness goes away. And don’t forget, unless they live near KFUPM, everybody is in the same boat!

________________ (See question 5.) Having English classes in English is bad enough, but having to study mathematics and physics in English as well? It might sound difficult now, but for most students it becomes normal after a few months. And don’t forget, it’s because you’re studying in English now that you’ll be able to understand all your lectures at the Jebel, where the professors come from all over the world!

Then there’s the last problem. At your high school, you were always the best in the class. And here at KFUPM? You’re just not the best in the class any more. So what’s the best advice for this one? Well, do what you’ve always done. Do your best. Do the best you can do. Nobody can ask for more than that.

title: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
paragraphs: Thailand is a wonderful place for a holiday. With its fascinating culture and wonderful beaches, there’s always something to keep any tourist satisfied. And if you’re keen on visiting traditional markets, the one we’d most recommend is Damnoen Saduak Market, often referred to as Bangkok’s Floating Market.

________________ (See question 3.) The market operates in the town of Damnoen Sadak, on a canal built on the orders of King Rama IV. Started in 1866 and finished in 1868, the canal was built to facilitate transport from nearby provinces to the town, which is 105 kilometres from Bangkok, in the province of Ratchapouri. The actual floating market opened in 1967.

So what can visitors expect? If you visit, you are sure to see the traditional Thai style of buying and selling. Every day, the canal is crowded by hundreds of boats belonging to vendors trying to get a good price for their fish, fruit, vegetables and just about anything else! During working hours, from around six until noon, Thai women wearing colourful bamboo hats sell exotic fruit and vegetables, which include carrots, onions, Malacca grapes, Chinese grapefruit, mangoes, bananas and coconuts. The air is full of the sights, sounds and smells of a traditional Thai market. It is always crowded, with both tourists and locals alike!

If you plan on visiting, there are a number of options open to you. If you take a regular bus from Bangkok, you will pay 50 baht and the journey takes two hours. Alternatively, you can pay around 550 baht for a guided tour direct from your hotel. These normally also include a boat trip out of the floating market and into the nearby countryside. Whatever you do, make sure you get there early, as the market gets very crowded later in the morning. For more information, visit our website www.visitthailand.com.

title: The History of Writing
paragraphs: According to historians, human civilization first began 12,000 years ago. This was in the historical country of Mesopotamia, which lies in what is now modern-day Iraq. At that time, people called the Sumerians started farming in the fertile land along the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, where it was easier to grow crops and keep farm animals. The Sumerians are famous as the world’s oldest known civilization. They are also famous for inventing the world’s first writing, which they did 5,000 years ago. With 870 separate words, Sumerian is the world’s first written language. There was one big problem with the Sumerian language, however. Because the Sumerians didn’t have paper, they could only write in stone, and stone is really heavy.

Another ancient civilization discovered the solution. 5,000 years ago, the Egyptians invented papyrus, a material like paper which they used for writing on. Papyrus was not heavy like stone: for the first time, people could easily carry what they wrote. The Egyptians made papyrus from the leaves of the papyrus plant. 7 years ago, scientists found the earliest ever example of papyrus at Wadi Al-Jarf on the Red Sea. The papyrus they found had a description of the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza from 4,500 years ago. Although papyrus was better for writing on than stone, it was still not perfect. It was easy to break, and was very often damaged by water. However, in the history of written language, there would be another great development, paper. And this time it was going to come from China.

________________ (See question 7.) He was a Chinese man called Cai Lun, who lived about 2,000 years ago. Cai Lun learned how to make paper from wood and water. Over the next 1,000 years, his invention spread from China to the rest of the world, reaching the Islamic world about 1,200 years ago. By the 11th century, papermaking had reached Europe; by the 13th century, there were paper mills that used waterwheels to make paper.

title: The Eiffel Tower
paragraphs: It is probably the most famous manmade structure on Earth. With a height of 324 metres, it was built using 18,038 different pieces of metal, and has a weight of 7,300 tonnes. To walk up it, you need to climb 1,665 steps. Until the completion of the Chrysler Building in New York in 1930, it was the highest structure in the world, and it is still the highest structure in Paris. Every night, it is lit up by 20,000 lightbulbs, so that it is visible from anywhere in the centre of the city. It is, of course, the Eiffel Tower.

________________ (See question 4.) It was then that an engineer called Maurice Koechlin came up with a plan for a great tower. He showed his plan to his boss, Gustave Eiffel. Eiffel loved the plan. At the same time, the French government was holding a competition, which was for the best design for a special building to inaugurate the 1889 Paris World Fair. Gustave Eiffel entered his plan for the competition. It won, and building work began on 28 January, 1887.

The main part of the work was completed in March 1889. On 31 March 1889, Gustave Eiffel took a group of important French politicians, journalists, businessmen and other dignitaries on a climb to the top. At 2:35 pm, he hoisted a large French flag to the top of the tower. 6 weeks later, on 6 May, the Paris World Fair opened, and 9 days after that, the tower finally opened to the general public. By 26 May, almost 30,000 people had climbed to the top. By the end of the World Fair, the tower had received 1,896,987 visitors.

If you’re planning a visit to the Eiffel Tower, here are some important details. Tickets are available online at www.ticket.toureiffel.paris. Adult tickets range in price from €10.20 to €25.50. The more you pay, the higher up you can go. In the higher price tickets, elevator access is included, but those on the cheaper option will be limited to the stairs only! In addition to these prices, a range of discounts for young people, students and the disabled are also available. The tower is open from 09:30 to 23:45 every day of the week. The peak period for visiting the tower is from July to September. During this period, the line can be extremely long so you will need to be patient!

title: Pocahontas
paragraphs: Nowadays, when most people hear the name Pocahontas, they think of the Disney movie. She is best-known as a character in a movie for children. But, unlike Snow White or the Lion King, there really was a person called Pocahontas. Like Crazy Horse, Sitting Bull and Sacagawea, she is among the most famous and important of history’s Native Americans. So who was the real Pocahontas?

________________ (See question 3.) She was born in about 1595 in Virginia. Her father was called Powhatan, and was the chief of his tribe. Like all members of her Algonquian-speaking tribe, she had several names. Early in life she was called Matoaka. Later, she was known as Amonute. By the time of her death, she was known as Rebecca Rolfe, but it is by the name Pocahontas that she became famous.

Pocahontas first came into contact with Europeans in 1607, when she met an Englishman called Captain John Smith. While Smith was exploring the Chickahominy River, Pocahontas’s brother, Opechancanough, took Smith and his men prisoner. Smith later said that Pocahontas saved his life. The Native Americans were going to kill him, he claimed, but Pocahontas stopped them. However, many historians dispute Smith’s story, saying that he had just misunderstood what was happening.

Later, war broke out between the Native Americans and the British. It was at this time that another British soldier, Captain Samuel Argall, took Pocahontas prisoner. But the British treated Pocahontas well. She learned to speak English, and then, on April 15, 1614, she married John Rolfe, a farmer and widower: his first wife had died on the journey from Britain to America. Pocahontas changed her name to Rebecca Rolfe. The husband and wife lived together for two years at Rolfe’s farm, which was where their son, Thomas Rolfe, was born.

Later in 1616, Pocahontas travelled to London, famous as an American princess. On January 5, 1617, she met King James II at his palace. But then, in March 1617, she fell ill with pneumonia. Pocahontas died on 21 March, 1617. She was just 22 years old.

title: Comparing Three British Capital Cities
paragraphs: The United Kingdom, or Britain, is actually an amalgamation of three separate countries, England, Scotland and Wales. Each of these has its own capital city, London for England, Cardiff for Wales and Edinburgh for Scotland. In this article, we’re going to draw a comparison between these three capitals, and ask a difficult question: which is the best to live in?

Cardiff is a large city, with an area of 140.3 square kilometres, but Edinburgh is bigger, with an area of 264 square kilometres. London, however, is much bigger than both Cardiff and Edinburgh, with an area of 1,572 square kilometres. London has the largest population as well. More than 8 million people live in London. Edinburgh’s population is a lot smaller than London’s. There are 464,990 people living in Edinburgh. This is a little larger than the population of Cardiff, which is 362,756.

________________ (See question 6.) Cardiff is the smallest city, with the fewest people, but it is very old. People first lived in London 2,000 years ago, when it was founded by the Romans. Edinburgh is a little older than London. People first lived in Edinburgh 2,850 years ago. But people first started living in Cardiff 8,000 years ago! It is much older than both London and Edinburgh.

So which is the best city to live in? That depends very much on your personal preferences, and what you are looking for. London is the richest city, so it might be the best for people looking for a good job. Because it is so far to the north, Edinburgh is the coldest and wettest city, so it might be better for people who like cold weather and the rain. So what can we say about Cardiff? Well, it’s the oldest city, so perhaps it is best for people who like history.

title: Dubai
paragraphs: Dubai is the largest and most populated city in the United Arab Emirates. Located on the south-east coast of the Arabian Gulf, it is famous throughout the world as a city for tourists to visit. And what makes it so famous? It could be its famous buildings. Dubai has some truly wonderful examples of architecture. There’s the Burj Al-Arab, the world’s only seven-star hotel. Then there’s the Jumeirah Palm Islands, the world’s largest artificial islands (built in 2001.) Finally, there’s the Burj Khalifa, at 828 metres the world’s tallest building. But there is something else that makes Dubai famous throughout the world: shopping.

________________ (See question 5.) Dubai Mall is the world’s largest and most visited shopping mall, with over half a million square metres of floor space. In 2014, more than 80 million visitors shopped at the mall’s 1,200 stores, which include world famous brands like Valentino, Gucci, Chanel and Ralph Lauren. And if shops alone aren’t enough, Dubai Mall is also home to the world’s largest aquarium and aquatic zoo!

Then there’s the Ibn Battuta Mall, the world’s largest themed shopping mall. Here, the mall is divided into six courts, each using historical architecture from around the world. There’s the India Court, the China Court, the Persia Court, the Egypt Court, the Tunisia Court and finally the Andalusia Court. It’s a shopping mall where shoppers can feel like explorers as they shop. But if you don’t like modern shopping malls, why not visit some of Dubai’s traditional souks?

title: The Worst Town in Britain
paragraphs: Britain has some beautiful towns and cities, and every year, there’s a competition to decide which is best. People vote for their favourite town or city. Usually, people choose famous places like London, Oxford or Cambridge. But there are also some places that never ever win.

The town of Drizzley, for example, has never won this competition. Drizzley, however, has won a very different competition. It has won the competition for Worst Town in Britain, and it has won this competition more than once. It won in 2007. It won again in 2008. It won again in 2009. Then it won in every year from then until (and including) 2019. Drizzley is famous for being the worst town in Britain. In the words of Drizzley resident Eric Smith, ‘Drizzley? It’s abysmal! Total rubbish!’ So what makes this town so bad?

________________ (See question 5.) Every day, the icy rain and freezing wind blow in from north, south, east and west. It’s colder, wetter and windier than anywhere else in Britain, and the sky is almost always a dark grey. Because of the weather, everybody walks round feeling depressed and sad all day. Everywhere else in the world has four seasons, summer, autumn, winter and spring, but Drizzley has just two: winter and July. How do people in Drizzley feel about the weather in Drizzley? They complain about it absolutely all of the time. So why don’t they move somewhere with better weather?

Because they’ve got no money. Once upon a time in Drizzley, there were factories, and people had jobs. Then the factories closed, and people stopped having jobs. Drizzley has Britain’s highest rate of unemployment, with about 40% of the adult population unemployed. Amongst people aged 18-24, there is 65% unemployment. Overall, only 48% of people in Drizzley have any kind of job, jobs like being supermarket security guards, street cleaners or taxi drivers, and for those people salaries are very low, about 70% of Britain’s average. There are a lot of poor people in Drizzley. And, unfortunately, sometimes poor people do bad things.

Drizzley is famous for having a lot of criminals. About 50% of the criminals have gone to prison, and the other 50% haven’t gone to prison yet. Never leave your car on the street at night, because it won’t be there the next morning. And, as well as all the crime, there are all the problems with pollution in Drizzley.

title: Edinburgh
paragraphs: Edinburgh is a very old and beautiful city. It is not the capital of the UK (that’s London) but it is the capital of Scotland, which is one of the countries in the UK. Edinburgh has a population of about 794,000 people, so it is not the biggest city in Scotland. The biggest city is Glasgow, with a population of about 1,655,000. However, Edinburgh is much older than Glasgow. Edinburgh lies on the east coast of Scotland, on the River Forth.

________________ (See question 4.) It became the capital of Scotland in about 1365. In 1707, the two countries of Scotland and England joined together to become the UK. Edinburgh was still the capital, but the king in London in England ruled Scotland. About 200 years ago, Edinburgh became an industrial city. Because of this, its population grew fast, but not as fast as Glasgow’s. In 1821, Glasgow became Scotland’s most populous city, and the UK’s fifth largest.

Nowadays, people in Edinburgh rule Scotland again, because Scotland has its own government. People in London do not rule Scotland now. Edinburgh is also a wealthy city. Apart from London, which is in first place, it is the wealthiest city in the UK. This is because it has many new companies. Edinburgh also has a very good university, which is one of the best in the UK.

If you visit Edinburgh, you can get there by train, plane or car. There are many hotels open all year round. Make sure you visit in the summer, because for most of the year Edinburgh is a very cold and wet city. There are plenty of things to see or do. You can visit the famous and beautiful Edinburgh Castle or walk along Princes Street. If you enjoy music or theatre, it is good to visit the Edinburgh Festival, which takes place for two weeks every June.

title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa
paragraphs: In 1592, the scientist Galileo Galilei climbed the 296 steps to the top of the tower. With him, he carried cannonballs. They were of different mass. This was because he was going to use them in an experiment, the purpose of which was to show that the speed objects fall at does not depend on their weight. The tower was a good place for Galileo to carry out his experiment. It was in his hometown, the Italian city of Pisa. It was also the tallest building for miles around. But the tower is not famous because of Galileo’s experiment.

________________ (See question 4.) With a lean angle of 3.97 degrees, it is, alongside the Eiffel Tower and the Egyptian Pyramids, amongst the most famous buildings in the world. It is the Leaning Tower of Pisa.

We do not know for sure who the tower’s architect was. For hundreds of years, people believed the tower was designed by Bonanno Pisano, a well-known resident of Pisa, who left Pisa for the Sicilian town of Monreale in 1185. However, historian Piero Pierotti’s study, published in 2001, said that the real architect was somebody called Diotisalvi. The study said that it was more likely to be him because, firstly, of when the tower was designed, and, secondly, because of its similarity to other towers designed by Diotisalvi.

On 5 January 1172, a woman called Donna Berta Di Bernado gave the town of Pisa a large amount of money (60 soldi). This money was used to buy the stones that would be used to build the tower. On 9 August 1173, builders dug the tower’s foundations, and on 14 August 1173, they began work on the ground floor. At this point, however, it was inevitable that the tower was going to lean. The foundations, at only three metres, were just not deep enough to support the tower’s weight. In 1178, the famous leaning began.

It would be another two hundred years before the tower was finished, but not because it was leaning. Pisa’s wars with other Italian city states, Genoa, Lucca and Florence, prevented work. On 12 April 1264, master builder Giovanni Di Simone and 23 workers went to the countryside near Pisa to cut stone. In 1272, building work began again, but the tower would not be finished until 1372.

title: Global Warming and the Greenhouse Effect
paragraphs: If the greenhouse effect stopped working today, we’d all die. Our planet’s average temperature would fall to -18 °C, and the oceans, seas and rivers would freeze.

________________ (See question 2.) It is a function of the gases around our planet that form the atmosphere. They let the Sun’s heat come to Earth, but stop some of it going back into space. Without these greenhouse gases, which include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and ozone, none of the heat from the Sun would stay on Earth. It would all go back into space. Our planet would be too cold to live on.

Nowadays, however, there is a big problem. The amounts of some greenhouse gases in the atmosphere are increasing. This means that less of the Sun’s heat leaves the Earth than before, and this is the cause of global warming and climate change.

The world is getting warmer. NASA records the weather. 16 of the 17 hottest years in the last 134 years have occurred since 2000. This rise in temperature is affecting the weather. Scientists believe that a range of extreme weather events, including tornadoes, hurricanes, floods, blizzards and wildfires, are happening because of an increase in global temperatures. More serious, however, is what will happen if we do not stop the world becoming warmer.

If average temperatures rise by 4°C, the ice at the North and South Poles will melt, and sea levels will rise. Cities that are now on the coast will disappear under the sea. This will include famous places like London, Bangkok, New York and Shanghai. The world will become so hot that farming and food production will often not be possible. Millions of people will starve. There will not be enough drinking water for everybody. Again, millions could die. Scientists predict a world full of war, hunger, pestilence and death. So how can we stop all this from happening?

title: Alexander Fleming and Penicillin
paragraphs: Alexander Fleming (6 August 1883 – 11 March 1955) is one of the most important figures in the history of medicine. His discovery of penicillin (the world’s first antibiotic) changed the way we treat disease. Thanks to his discovery, diseases such as tuberculosis and gangrene became treatable, where previously they had caused death.

________________ (See question 2.) On the morning of 23 September, 1928, he was tidying up his laboratory because it was cluttered. As he cleared up his equipment, he noticed what had happened to his glass plates. These glass plates had, as part of Fleming’s research, been covered with bacteria called Staphylococcus.

One of these plates, however, had mould growing on it. The mould (a type of substance that grows on old cheese or bread when left too long) seemed to have affected the bacteria. Fleming decided it had been killed by something in the mould. Fleming had always been interested in ways of killing bacteria. The mould on the glass plate was a type called penicillium notatum. Following further research, he discovered that it could kill other bacteria. It could also be given to animals without negative effects.

Fleming did not continue studying the mould, as there were other medical issues he needed to study. It was not until ten years later, in 1938, that Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, working at Oxford University, found the substance in the mould that killed bacteria. In 1941, they gave it to a patient whose wound had become infected. At first, the wounded patient got better, but after three weeks died because they had too little penicillin. However, they gave it to an American drugs company to mass-produce. By 1944, it was in common use. In 1945, Fleming, Florey and Chain were awarded the Nobel Prize. The era of antibiotics had begun.

title: Finding a Mammoth
paragraphs: The Russian region of Yamal-Nenet is home to the Nenet people. With an area of 750,300 km², and a population of 650,000, it is located in northwestern Siberia and is mostly surrounded by the Arctic Ocean. Its economy depends on its exports of oil, gold and fish, and, thanks to the Nenet people, it is famous for animals that became extinct 10,000 years ago: mammoths.

________________ (See question 6.) They have been digging them out of the ground for thousands of years. About two hundred years ago, the Nenet people began making money by selling the ivory from mammoths. Mammoths even play a part in the Nenet people’s beliefs and superstitions, with a fairy-tale creature called the mamont. The Nenet even believe that it is bad luck to find a mammoth, and that anybody who finds one will die because of their discovery.

It was good luck for science, however, that in May 2007 a Nenet farmer called Yuri Khudi found a mammoth on the bank of the Yurebei River. The mammoth, which had died 40,000 years previously, was in almost perfect condition. Instead of keeping the mammoth to sell its ivory, Yuri Khudi reported his find to a local museum. But when Yuri Khudi was taken by helicopter to show museum staff his find, it had disappeared.

Yuri’s cousin had sold the mammoth to a local shop owner. When the museum staff found it, on sale at the side of his shop, it had been damaged (stray dogs had bitten it). However, the local police forced the shop owner to turn it over to the museum staff, who flew it back to the museum. Although 40,000 years old, it is the best-preserved mammoth ever found. The museum staff called it Lyuba.

title: Hannibal
paragraphs:
________________ (See question 2.)
Hannibal, son of Hamilcar Barca, (248–183 BCE), was a soldier of the Carthaginian Empire. Many believe that he was one of the greatest leaders and soldiers in history.

________________ (See question 3.)
2,300 years ago, two great empires existed in North Africa and Europe: the Carthaginian Empire and the Roman Empire. The Carthaginian Empire was centred around Carthage, which is nowadays a suburb of the Tunisian capital, Tunis. It ruled North Africa, Sicily, Sardinia and much of Spain. The Roman Empire, controlling most of Italy and Corsica, was smaller, but it was growing. In 241 BCE, the Romans took Sicily from the Carthaginians. It was at this time that Hamilcar Barca, who had fought against the Romans, made his 7-year-old son, Hannibal, promise to hate the Romans for the rest of his life.

Hannibal The Soldier
19 years later, Hannibal became the leader of the Carthaginian Army, chosen because of his intelligence and bravery. As leader, he wanted one thing: to destroy the Roman Empire before it destroyed the Carthaginian Empire. But how was he to invade Italy across the Mediterranean Sea? The Carthaginians did not have enough ships to carry all his troops to Italy and invade by sea. Nobody could have imagined what Hannibal did next.

The Invasion 
________________ (See question 7.) He decided to take his army 2,400 kilometres on foot from Spain, over the Pyrenees Mountains, through the South of France and over the Alps, the mountains between Italy and the rest of Europe. He left Spain in 218 BCE with an army of 35,000 soldiers and a group of army elephants. In early spring, 217 BCE, he took his army over the Alps. Because of the winter conditions, he lost many of his elephants and thousands of his men. However, many soldiers hostile to Rome joined his army, and his numbers rose to about 40,000. He soon won a victory over the Romans at Cannae, killing 25,000 Romans.

________________ (See question 10.)
Hannibal’s invasion of the Roman Empire was not, however, to succeed. In the end, Hannibal was forced to give up his invasion when the Roman general Scipio invaded Carthage. Because of the danger, Hannibal had to leave Italy to defend the capital of the Carthaginian Empire. It was here that Hannibal was finally defeated. At the battle of Zama, Hannibal’s army was destroyed, and with it, Hannibal’s dream of destroying the Roman Empire.

title: Why the British Drive on the Left
paragraphs: They’re eccentric people, the British. They say sorry all the time, even when they’ve done nothing wrong. They talk about almost nothing but the weather and they always drink tea at five o’clock. Strangest of all is this: they drive on the wrong side of the road. Or rather: they do not drive on the right side of the road. They drive on the left. This article explains why the British just had to be different to everybody else.

________________ (See question 3.) It started way back before then. In fact, it goes back to the Roman Empire. In those days, the roads weren’t safe. Not because of traffic accidents, but because of robbers and thieves. When people travelled by horse, they carried swords so they could fight any attackers. Most people are right-handed, so naturally they carry swords in their right hands (see diagram 1). And, if you were riding on the left side of the road, it was much easier to fight your attacker. As a result, it became habit to ride on the left. This eventually became Roman law.

When they invaded, the Romans brought their law to Britain. In 1998, near the British town of Swindon, an old Roman road was discovered. The road had two lanes, a left and a right lane, and it led to a quarry, which is a place from which we cut stone. Now the left-hand lane was badly damaged, but the right-hand lane was hardly damaged at all. The damage to the left-hand lane was caused by very heavy horse-drawn carts (see diagram 2) which had been loaded with quarried stone (see diagram 3). This is how we know that when the horse-drawn carts drove away from the quarry, they drove on the left. Carts coming back to the quarry were much lighter, and so did no damage. The British habit of driving on the left is at least 2,000 years old.

So why does most of the world drive on the right? In eighteenth century Europe and America, horsemen did not carry swords. They carried whips, and their carts usually had two horses side-by-side. They carried these whips in their right hands, so it was easier to whip both horses if you sat on the left. Sitting on the left, it was easier to see the vehicles coming towards you when you drove on the right. And that’s why most of the world drives on the right.

title: Piracy and Its Golden Age
paragraphs: Piracy is as old as sea trade itself. As long as valuable goods have been traded by ship, pirates have attempted to steal them, with the first recorded example taking place in the Mediterranean 3,400 years ago. There is piracy in the present day too. It is common in the Indian Ocean, off the coast of Somalia, and in the South China Sea. Every year, piracy accounts for between $13 and $16 billion dollars of lost trade.

However, the time and place when piracy flourished most was in the Caribbean Sea from 1660 to 1726. It was during this period that piracy was at its height. It was this period that has given us many of our legends and stories about pirates. This might be why this period is called the Golden Age of Piracy.

________________ (See question 5.) After Columbus’s discovery of America in 1492, Spanish traders, seamen and soldiers flocked to the Caribbean. They had heard of the native American Incas’ gold and other riches, and wanted to steal it for themselves. Soon, Spanish sailing ships, heavily laden with gold, jewels, silk and expensive spices started making the sea voyage back to Spain from ports in the Caribbean. Word spread about these Spanish ships and their treasures. To many pirates and other criminals, robbing the slow-moving Spanish ships seemed an easy way to get rich quick. Thousands of pirates sailed to the Caribbean. From 1660 to 1724, the Caribbean was full of pirates hunting for the treasures being transported to Spain. It was piracy’s Golden Age.

Who were these pirates? While there were pirates such as Sir Henry Morgan and Blackbeard, who became famous for the exciting and adventurous lives they led, most were simply poor men trying to escape a difficult life. Many were Africans, who had been taken to work as slaves, and who had run away from the harsh conditions on slave ships. Others were ordinary sailors. In those times, conditions of life on trading ships were awful. The work was desperately hard and unhealthy, with very low pay. Sailors could be punished harshly for anything they did wrong. For men like these, life on a pirate ship looked very attractive. There were even two female pirates, Anne Bonney and Mary Read. But this was very uncommon because most sailors believed it was unlucky to have women on ships.
In the 1720s, however, the navies of different countries began to hunt down and kill the pirates of the Caribbean. By 1724, there were almost no pirates left. The Golden Age of Piracy was over.

title: Blackbeard and His Pirate Ship
paragraphs: On 21 November, 1996, divers exploring about one mile off the coast of North Carolina made an amazing discovery. There, located at 34°41′44″N 76°41′20″W, at a depth of 8.5 metres, they found the wreck of a sailing ship. The ship, historians realised, had belonged to the pirate Blackbeard. What was more, it was full of Blackbeard’s treasure.

Even though Blackbeard is history’s most notorious pirate, we know little of his early life. Named Edward Teach, he was probably born around 1680 in the British city of Bristol. It is likely that, as a young man, he was in the British navy, and fought at sea against the French. Some people believe that he fought during the War of the Spanish Succession (1701-1713).

What is known for sure is that he was active as a pirate in 1716. The following year, on November 17, 1717, he and his pirate band captured La Concorde, a French ship used for carrying slaves from Africa to the Americas. Blackbeard realised that La Concorde would be a great pirate’s ship. He changed its name to the Queen Anne’s Revenge, and armed it with 40 cannon, making it a powerful warship. Next, he set off along the Caribbean and North American coasts, plundering and killing as he went. In May, 1718, he robbed the city of Charleston on the coast of North Carolina. Finally, in June 1718, the Queen Anne’s Revenge sank about a mile offshore from Beaufort, North Carolina. Although Blackbeard and his crew managed to escape to land, the ship would lie hidden until 1996.

________________ (See question 8.) What he and his crew did to the city of Charleston had made the people there very angry. They sent a fleet of ships to hunt him down and kill him. On 22 November, 1718, after hours of battle offshore from North Carolina’s Outer Banks region, forces led by Lieutenant Robert Maynard killed Blackbeard and members of his crew. They cut Blackbeard’s head off and stuck it on a spike at the front of the ship.

As for the Queen Anne’s Revenge, it is now the subject of a new battle. This time, it is a legal battle, between the United States government and modern-day pirates: lawyers. The battle is about who the treasure on Blackbeard’s ship belongs to. Some things just never change.

title: Thomas Edison and His Inventions
paragraphs: Thomas Edison (February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) is one of the greatest inventors in history. During his life, he invented an amazing 1,093 different machines.

________________ (See question 3.) He went to school for a short time but his marks were very bad. He had problems with reading and writing. His teachers thought he was crazy. They told his mother there was something wrong with him. So his mother decided to keep him at home. His mother taught him to read and write. In 1859, when he was 12, he got a job selling newspapers on trains. He made a lot of money. When he was 15, he started his own newspaper. Again, he made a lot of money by peddling it on trains.

In 1869, when Edison was 22, he moved to New York. He got a job working for a gold company. One day, the gold company’s printing machine broke down. Edison fixed it, and then invented a printing machine that worked better. Edison’s printing machine was not his first invention, but it was the first that became successful. It made him a lot of money. His next famous invention was the phonograph, a machine which could record and play sounds. Edison thought that it was a good toy for children.

Edison is most famous for the electric light bulb. The electric light bulb was not his invention (that was Joseph Swan in Britain in 1875), but he did make it work better. In 1880, Edison made a 16-watt light bulb that could work for 1,500 hours. He also invented a way of making electricity and giving it to all the houses in a town. In the 1890s, for the first time in history, many towns had electric light. At the end of Edison’s life, most cities in the world had electric light. Edison had changed the world.
He died in 1931 at the age of 84.
